H1 remains the only hypothesis consistent with the verified evidence. Temporal order is now tight: dep-6010 at 07:40:00Z, first settlement-service deserialize error at 07:42:14Z (2m14s later), lag inflection at the 07:40 bucket and request_rate collapse at 07:45 — cause precedes onset, and the only competing change (cfg-3004, 07:35) is contradicted by content-specific failure evidence (F16). H2/H3/H4 are each contradicted by verified findings, not merely dismissed (F10/F11/F16 for H2; F28/F17/F25/F3 for H3; F10/F11/F12/F7/F8 for H4). Alternatives were enumerated across all services, not just the reported one (F2/F20/F22/F23): order-service and payment-service are the only producers on 'orders', and payment-service has zero changes in the window.

The blocking issue from round 1 was H1's load-bearing origin hop — that offset orders-3@8841207 was produced by order-service. Round 2 (T4) returned a confirmed negative: no producer→topic/partition mapping exists in the tooling (F24, tc-030/tc-023), so the hop remains supported by correlation (2-min adjacency plus exact schema vocabulary) rather than observation. The promised cheap closing checks were attempted and partially answered: notification-service shows no deserialize failure (F29), but the per-consumer sweep across other 'orders' consumers was cut off by budget exhaustion, and per-partition lag was never obtainable (group-level aggregate only, F30). Notably, the absence of the signature on one consumer is NOT evidence about the topic-wide blast radius, and the round-2 attempt to broaden it failed for budget rather than unavailability — so this remains outstanding, not permanently unobtainable.

Two distinct, obtainable questions remain that could change the fix: (a) whether the producer itself emitted the v2 record on orders-3 (order-service publish/log correlation at the poison offset), and (b) whether the failure is producer-side/shared or consumer-specific (other 'orders' consumers). Both are answerable with the remaining 22 tool calls. Because (a)/(b) decide whether the remediation is revert/upgrade the producer, upgrade the consumer, or patch consumer poison-message handling, I cannot accept at 0.75+ yet, but this is NOT inconclusive — the data do separate H1 from H2/H3/H4; only the producer-identity sub-hop and blast radius remain open. Confidence capped at 0.75, same as round 1, because nothing new closed the load-bearing hop.

Scope caveat worth recording as an assumption, not a blocker: F4/F20 establish kafka's shared nature and the 'orders' producer/consumer set, but edges carry no topic names, so "order-service and settlement-service meet on orders/orders-3" is still graph-inferred. H3 is weakened but not positively disproven (no broker/DB telemetry exists at all), which is why the cap is not raised.

critiques.summary:
FINAL ROUND. H1 is the only hypothesis consistent with verified evidence, and it is accepted with a capped confidence of 0.72 rather than 0.75, because its one load-bearing hop remains circumstantial.

What is verified and load-bearing: (1) Onset is established tightly — dep-6010 order-service v2.16.0 live 07:40:00Z, and the sharpest onset marker, settlement-service's first deserialize ERROR at 07:42:14Z ('failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'), 2m14s later; lag inflects in the 07:40 bucket (F9/F30) and request_rate collapses ~62→0.4 req/s by 07:45 (F10). Cause precedes onset tightly. (2) The failure is content-specific: 409 ERRORs, 100% on orders-3@8841207, exactly two patterns — schema mismatch (213x) and poison-message/partition-blocked retry with attempt counters in the tens of thousands (196x, F7/F8/F26/F27). A fixed offset retried 92k times explains the ~0.4 req/s floor and monotonic lag without any broker/DB/volume story. (3) The deploy's declared change vocabulary ('rename qty -> quantity', 'event schema version header v2') matches the consumer error verbatim, and dep-6010 is the only deployment anywhere in the fleet window (F2/F14/F23) with the only deployed service that emits OrderExecuted (F18/F21).

Alternatives are contradicted by verified evidence, not merely dismissed: H2 (cfg-3004) cannot produce a per-message deserialize failure or a blocked partition from a batch-size change (F16), and is 7m14s before onset; H3 (broker/DB) fails on the absence of any rebalance/assignment log text (F28, 0 matches) and the content-specific signature, though broker/DB telemetry is permanently absent so it stays weakened-not-zeroed; H4 (volume burst) predicts gradual degradation, whereas the evidence shows a near-total halt with CPU pinned and no 5xx (F10/F11/F12); H5 is contradicted by corroborated error logs at a fixed offset.

The unresolved hop, stated honestly: no producer-side publish log or partition mapping exists anywhere in the tooling (F24/F36/F38/F39/F40, tc-043/055), so 'order-service produced orders-3@8841207' rests on 2-minute adjacency plus exact schema-vocabulary match. T6's bounded search returned an explicit negative, and T4/T8 confirmed no per-partition lag series exists. This is a permanent data-source limitation, not a missing query — which is why it is a confidence cap and an assumption, not grounds for more evidence or for 'inconclusive'.

Why not 'inconclusive': the surviving uncertainty does not separate hypotheses naming different origins. H3/H4 name different origins (broker/DB event; volume burst) and are each contradicted by verified content-specific evidence; the residual risk is that a silent, unrecorded broker/DB event coincidentally coincides with the schema error, which no available or unavailable data source can positively exclude and which does not change the leading conclusion. The one genuinely open sub-question — producer shipped uncoordinated v2 vs. consumer is stale v1 — names the SAME origin (the uncoordinated OrderExecuted v2 schema change from dep-6010) and the SAME causal chain; both readings are fixed by reverting/coordinating the producer or by upgrading the consumer, so it does not flip the ranking or the fault origin. It lowers confidence; it does not make the analysis inconclusive. With zero tool calls remaining and the decisive data sources confirmed absent, continued investigation costs outage minutes for no ranking change.

Recommended action given the cap: treat the OrderExecuted v2 schema change from dep-6010 as the origin, and mitigate on the producer side (revert/coordinate dep-6010 or add v1-compatible emission), since that is the reversible direction and the only change in the window; if the settlement consumer's poison-message handling can be patched to skip-and-quarantine the failed offset, that unblocks partition orders-3 immediately and is safe under either reading.

The claim that order-service's v2 producer wrote orders-3@8841207 rests only on 2m14s timing adjacency plus exact schema-vocabulary match. T6 returned an explicit negative. This is a permanent data limitation, not an outstanding query.

Scope confinement unverified: no partition-dimensioned lag or commit metric exists for the settlement consumer group or kafka (F32/F34/F35, T8). The group aggregate is consistent with a single blocked partition OR fleet-wide lag, so 'stall confined to orders-3' is corroborated only by log-embedded partition tags (orders-3@8841207), not by a lag series.

Cross-service blast radius not demonstrated: only notification-service was checked and returned zero (F29); the per-consumer sweep over payment-service/exchange-gateway/ledger-db/portfolio-service/market-data-service returned zero matches but only for the exact signature strings queried, and lag/request-rate checks for all of them were never run (budget_exhausted). A producer-side/shared fault therefore cannot be positively confirmed by multiple consumers failing; the five zero-matches are hard negatives for the probed signature strings only.

Unverified assumption retained: order-service and settlement-service are assumed to meet on the same topic 'orders'/partition orders-3, because graph edges (F4/F20) carry no topic or partition names. If they do not, H1's mechanism has no shared medium — the residual alternative this leaves open (a silent broker/DB event, H3) cannot be excluded because broker/ledger-db telemetry does not exist at all.

H3's exclusion rests partly on absence of evidence: no per-partition produce metric, no kafka consumer_lag, no broker resource series, and no per-service config/deploy query confirmed empty for kafka/ledger-db individually (GAP: tool budget). Zero rebalance/assignment log matches (F28) is keyword-search absence, weaker than a direct group-state observation. H3 is weakened and demoted, not positively disproven — consistent with the cap, but it means a silent broker event coinciding with the schema error cannot be formally excluded.
